triage.why: _transfer caches both balances before writing, so a self-transfer of 50 shares credits the sender 50 extra shares without changing totalSupply, which creates shares from nothing.

The allowance is type(uint256).max, which by the standard (and this code) means unlimited and is not spent; the family rule should have excluded the max allowance, as my custom transferfrom_allowance rule does.
The K check compares balances scaled by 10_000 against reserves scaled by only 1000**2, so it is 100x too lax: 50 wei of token1 buys 99% of the token0 reserve and x*y collapses.
Same mis-scaled K check: a 100-wei donation lets the caller drain 990e18 of token0, lowering x*y.
Same mis-scaled K check: 2 wei of token0 buys almost half the token1 reserve, so the value per LP share falls for every LP.
skim(to = the pair itself) sends the excess back to the pair, a harmless no-op that leaves the balance above the reserve; my rule wrongly assumed skim always reduces balances to the reserves.

deposit sets rewardDebt from the old amount (0 for a new staker) and then adds the stake, so the newcomer's debt stays 0 and they can harvest all rewards accumulated since launch on the new stake, draining earlier stakers' rewards.
deposit is cast to uint128, so a large rate*duration is silently truncated: the creator escrows far less than the stream promises, while streamed() pays the full rate out of other streams' funds.
